rules: Bullet points should be grammatically complete sentences.
Do not use full stops at the end of bullet points.
Follow an "Impact Word + What + Effect + How" structure for bullet points.
Quantify your points as much as possible using numbers and percentages.
Highlight the business or technical impact you made (e.g., % increase in efficiency, hours saved, % output increase, % waste decrease).
Avoid repeating action words across the resume.
Ensure bullet points fit on a single line. Avoid 2-line points or 1.5-line points; ensure sub-points complete a single line.
Avoid explaining too much in a single point; focus on the outcome.
Keep information short and to the point.
Keep usage of italics minimal; do not use them in points.
Ensure all headings and bullet points start at the same vertical location.
Organize sub-points sequentially, or with the most impactful/important first.
Utilize the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) framework for documenting project progress.
For Professional/Research Experience, detail responsibilities (team, role, aim), methods (platforms, equipment, software), and quantifiable impact.
For Technical/Key Projects, explain completed work, mention software, algorithms, libraries, and achieved efficiency/results.
For Positions of Responsibility, quantify team/budget size, number of people/students affected, describe your role, unique contributions, new initiatives, and the effect of your work.
